proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 40, 12^n is congruent to 12^(n mod 6) modulo 19.

argument.text: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 34, 12^(n+6) mod 19 is congruent to 12^(n) mod 19 modulo 19.
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 40, n^2 is at least 2*n.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 40 for which n^2 > 13.
For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 40, at least one of the following holds: n mod 6 = 0; n mod 6 = 1; n mod 6 = 2; n mod 6 = 3; n mod 6 = 4; n mod 6 = 5.
For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 40, if n mod 6 = 0 then 12^(n) mod 19 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, at least one of the following holds: n mod 3 = 0; n mod 3 = 1; n mod 3 = 2.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 40, n^2 + n is congruent to (n^2 + n) + 221 modulo 13.
The steps above establish the statement up to 40, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 40.
